content.text:
The merged code tells a clear story. Let me record the key branch-reality findings before moving on:

- **#37**: Oliver's concerns *were* addressed on-branch — the `Locked` serialized field was replaced with `IsLocked => !ComboManager...IsComboUnlocked(Id)`, the enum was renamed to `ERarityEnum`, and the prefab was consolidated. Author also won the `_specialPrefab` naming argument (renamed to `SpecialComboCell`). No formal re-approval, but code was fixed.
- **#35**: rename landed (file gone from `Assets/Store/DominoPlayerPrefs.cs`), `private` added — but the "dangerous `_statPrefab` GameObject/GetComponent" concern was **not** addressed; it's still an untyped `GameObject` with an unguarded `GetComponent<ProfileStat>()` → live NRE risk.
- **#26**: **zero commits after the review** — the monetization/design objection (cooldown resets on loss → lose-fast exploit) shipped untouched.
- **#19**: Oliver fixed it himself ("fixing null refs") — the index-out-of-range concern was resolved before merge.

Now let me find the design spec Owen referenced and the Linear engineering board.

content.text: The design workbook is revealing: the **"Combo List"** sheet has **no rarity column and no unlock-cost column**, and the only "level multiplier" table (Combo Sheet) is for **tile** levels (1→1, 2→2.5, 3→6, 4→14, 5→32), not combo-rarity unlock costs. That's directly relevant to Owen's spec doubt. Let me confirm against the GDD and Confluence before concluding.

content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"Overview\\n\\n### 1. Game Overview\\nTitle: Combo Fighter\\nGenre: Merge puzzle auto battler\\nPlatform: (iOS / Android)\\nCore Loop Summary:\\nPlace fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.\\n### 2. Core Gameplay\\nPlayer Actions:\\nDrag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.\\nDraw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.\\nGain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.\\nWhen the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.\\nGame Objective:\\nDefeat all the waves of monsters in each level.\\nFailure Condition:\\nThe player\\u2019s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.\\n### 3. Game Flow\\nHome Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.\\nGameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.\\nResult Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.\\nUpgrades: Hero\\u2019s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero\\u2019s attack power bonus\\n### 4. Level Design\\n35 hand crafted levels in MVP\\nMonsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.\\nLevels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.\\nLevels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.\\n### 5. Art & Visual Style\\nThe top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.\\nDuring intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.\\nCharacter Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.\\nUI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.\\n### 6. Audio\\nMusic: None\\nSFX: Standard fighting sounds.\\n### 7. Monetization\\nAds: None in MVP\\n### 8. Ugly Game Mockups\\nHome Screen with 3 upgrade choices, start button, coin balance and settings button\\n\\nGameplay\\n\\nGame Starts, 3 pieces randomly selected for players to choose from.\\nPlayers drag pieces onto the board, the character starts doing loop animation of the attacks on the board.\\nThe values showing total punch, kick and special attack power changes real time based on pieces on the board\\nThe dmg/s calculation also updates real time as pieces are being placed\\nThe Info button will bring up a pop up of available moves (see below)\\nPressing refresh will consume gold if available, and refreshes the 3 cards.\\nHolding a tile under the finger will change the refresh button to SELL. If a player moves pieces over the sell button, the piece will be sold.\\nCoin balance and health is displayed near the top\\nAfter pressing the fight button, the camera shifts upward to increase the size of the fight scene and the battle starts. This phase requires no input action from the players\\nInfo Pop Up\\n\\nSimple End Game Screen\\n\\n\\nDOCUMENT DOES NOT END HERE! MAKE SURE TO CLICK ON THE OTHER TABS (\\u201cDetailed Mechanics\\u201d) IN THIS DOCUMENT ON THE LEFT SIDE BAR IN GOOGLE DOCS\\n\\n\\nDetailed Mechanics\\n### 1. Starting A Level\\nLevel starts with a 6x6 empty game board.\\nThe level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.\\n\\nPlayers are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.\\n\\nTiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.\\nOnce the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 Special attack (fireball) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 repeat\\n\\nWhen the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.\\n\\nIf There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)\\n\\nFireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.\\nPlayers will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.\\n\\nWhen the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.\\nThe game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.\\nPLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..\\n\\n#### Block Merging & Rearrangement\\nWhen the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.\\nHolding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.\\nWhen the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.\\nLike the video below.\\nScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4\\nWhile arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.\\nThe only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.\\nOnce players decide to continue fighting, clicking the \\u201cFight\\u201d button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.\\nPlayers can merge the blocks in the bottom part.\\n### 2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation\\nThere are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.\\n\\nTiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.\\n\\nTiles will come in different shapes\\n\\nPunch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40\\n\\nThe same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called \\u201cAssist Tiles,\\u201d they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.\\n\\nThe individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.\\n\\n\\n\\nThe damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:\\n\\n[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier\\nThis calculates the individual action power for the combo\\n\\nCombo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.\\n\\n\\n\\nSmall sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.\\n\\n\\n\\n### 3. Combo Creation UI/UX\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n### 4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades\\nThere will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.\\nThey will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. ### 1. Game Overview
Title: Combo Fighter
Genre: Merge puzzle auto battler
Platform: (iOS / Android)
Core Loop Summary:
Place fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.
### 2. Core Gameplay
Player Actions:
Drag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.

Gain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.

Game Objective:
Defeat all the waves of monsters in each level.
Failure Condition:
The player’s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.
### 3. Game Flow
Home Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.
Gameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.
Result Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.

35 hand crafted levels in MVP

The top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.
During intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.

UI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.

Music: None
SFX: Standard fighting sounds.

Detailed Mechanics
### 1. Starting A Level
Level starts with a 6x6 empty game board.
The level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.

Players are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.

Tiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.
Once the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) → 0.6 second delay → Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) → 0.6 second delay → Special attack (fireball) → 0.6 second delay → repeat

When the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.

If There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)

Fireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.
Players will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.

When the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.
The game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.
PLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..

#### Block Merging & Rearrangement
When the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.
Holding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.
When the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.
Like the video below.
ScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4
While arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.
The only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.
Once players decide to continue fighting, clicking the “Fight” button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.
Players can merge the blocks in the bottom part.
### 2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation
There are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.

Tiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.

Tiles will come in different shapes

Punch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40

The same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called “Assist Tiles,” they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.

The individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.



The damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:

[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier
This calculates the individual action power for the combo

Combo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.

### 3. Combo Creation UI/UX




### 4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades
There will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.
They will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.
Attack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)
Health Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp
Health Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.
### 5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot
Each monster when hit is “stunned” for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.
Monster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp
We do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP
When monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP
Monster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.


### 6. Levels
We need to let designers designate starting positions for each level.
Each level will also have obstacles that need to be removed via silver.

Each level will have 15 waves of monsters
Each wave of monsters will get an HP and damage multiplier bonus following a standard algorithm
HP multiplier for monster is wave # * XXX
Damage multiplier for monster is wave # * YYY
We need to utilize the monster spawning system from Zombie Match, this will allow designers to specify monsters spawn timing and quantity
#### Level Design Tools
Each level will have monsters, monsters spawn, their stats, board type, and the pool of tiles available.
So what’s needed from a level is that

Start and exit nodes  (if necessary later on)
### 7. Player Starting Stats
Base player HP is 100
Base player regen rate is 2% per second, but this is only during the “fight” phase and not the prep phase.
Base attack is 0, no tiles placed = no damage.

For Silver Tables Combo Fighter Design Details

Experience points will reset after each attempt, meaning that it will start from the scratch in every level attempt.
Experience will be gained from the actions below,
Merging blocks yield less XP
Killing enemies yields more XP
Roguelite skills don't require any currency to use. Just selecting the desired one out of all 3 options.
The skills will have 3 phases that can be improved further after selecting the first phase.

But since combo-unlocking is a monetization feature, let me check the SHOP deck before concluding, as it's the one place an unlock spec could plausibly live.

Confirmed across every design source: the SHOP deck covers store items and a "Recommended Next Combo" feature but has **no combo rarity, unlock cost, or per-rarity leveling** either. So the shipped combo-rarity/unlock/leveling system (PR #37) has **no backing in any written spec** — GDD, Design Details workbook, SHOP deck, or Confluence. It traces only to an informal Slack brainstorm.

I now have everything. Let me record my plan and execute: 4 Linear tickets (ENG, unassigned) + 4 PR comments + the Slack summary.

input.title: [Repo-state audit] PR #37 "Combo Definition Updates" merged without reviewer sign-off
input.description:
Recorded as part of the Combo-Fighters freeze audit (Arthur's request, before tooling access ends 2026-03-03). Combo Fighter is live and taking money; this records the state of the repo, not a commitment to fix.

**Repo:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters — PR #37, merged 2026-02-13 (base `develop`).
**Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks (CHANGES_REQUESTED, 2026-02-12). **Author:** the gameplay engineer (PERSON_5877). **No approval was ever recorded after the changes were requested.**

**What the reviewer pushed back on (files + asks):**
- `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboDefinition.cs` — `Locked` should not be a serialized field; use a PlayerPrefs/manager-backed availability check + `Unlock()`. Also `LevelMultiplierRow` class unnecessary (use a `float[]`). Enum should be prefixed `ERarityEnum`.
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/ComboScreen.cs` — `_specialPrefab` naming questioned (`_lockedPrefab`?).
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/LockedComboCell.cs` — replace function-per-rarity with a `SerializedDictionary<RarityEnum, ComboCellRarityData>`.
- `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboRarityData.cs` / `ComboRarityDefinition.cs` — "Is this used?" / "Why exactly do we need this?"

**What actually landed on the branch (checked at merge SHA bf4e630):**
- ✅ Most code feedback WAS addressed in follow-up commits ("Addressed PR review", etc.): the `Locked` field is gone (now `IsLocked => !ComboManager.Instance.IsComboUnlocked(Id)`), the enum is `ERarityEnum`, and the prefab was consolidated to a single `SpecialComboCell`.
- The `_specialPrefab` naming was an **argued-and-resolved** point — the author explained the cell is also used by non-common unlocked combos, and it was renamed `SpecialComboCell` (not ignored).

**Unresolved:**
1. **No reviewer ever re-reviewed/approved** after the changes — nobody confirmed the fixes; merged on the author's word.
2. **Design support:** `ComboRarityDefinition` (per-rarity unlock + level-up requirements, `UnlockCost` default 300) was justified in review as coming from "Combo Unlocking Specs". That spec could **not** be found in the GDD, the "Combo Fighter Design Details" workbook, the SHOP deck, or Confluence — see separate spec-mismatch note. The shipped enum also dropped `Common` (final commit "Removed Common rarity"), which contradicts the numbers the author quoted.

input.title: [Repo-state audit] PR #35 "Blake/backend" merged without sign-off — untyped _statPrefab GetComponent still live
input.description:
Recorded as part of the Combo-Fighters freeze audit (Arthur's request, before tooling access ends 2026-03-03). Records state; not a commitment to fix.

**Repo:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters — PR #35, merged 2026-01-30 21:33 (base `develop`).
**Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks (CHANGES_REQUESTED, 20:36). **Author:** Arthur Blake, who self-merged ~1 min after the last commit. **No approval recorded after the changes were requested.** (CodeRabbit also posted many actionable items on the AWS/Apple auth SDK — see PR.)

**Human review points (files + asks) and what landed (checked at merge SHA f065d1c):**
- `Assets/Store/DominoPlayerPrefs.cs` — "Can we rename this to something else?" Author replied "Yes". ✅ Landed — file no longer exists at that path (renamed).
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/Profile/ProfileScreen.cs` — "missing `private`". ✅ Landed (fields are private).
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/Profile/ProfileScreen.cs` — **"Looks dangerous"**: `_statPrefab` is a raw `GameObject`; if the prefab lacks a `ProfileStat` it gets instantiated and ignored. Reviewer asked to type it as `ProfileStat` and drop the `GetComponent`. ❌ **NOT addressed** — `_statPrefab` is still `GameObject` and `AddStat` still does `go.GetComponent<ProfileStat>()` then `stat.Init(...)` **with no null guard**, so a misconfigured prefab now throws a NullReferenceException at runtime (Profile screen). This objection is still standing in the live build.

Category: mixed — two points agreed & landed; one substantive point silently not addressed and live.

input.title: [Repo-state audit] PR #26 "Upgrade-ad cooldown" merged with design objection standing — lose-fast exploit live
input.description:
Recorded as part of the Combo-Fighters freeze audit (Arthur's request, before tooling access ends 2026-03-03). Records state; not a commitment to fix. **This one is a live monetization concern.**

**Repo:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters — PR #26, merged 2026-01-15 17:28 (base `develop`).
**Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks (CHANGES_REQUESTED, 13:36). **Author:** gameplay engineer (PERSON_5877). **No approval recorded after review.**

**What the reviewer pushed back on (files + asks):**
- Top-level design concern: the upgrade-ad cooldown should be time-based, AND he flagged the exploit — "the player can enter the level, lose very quickly and return to main menu and then they will be able to watch another ad and level up again."
- `Assets/Scripts/Managers/GameController.cs` — the cooldown reset (`Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset:true)`) should move to WinScreen so it doesn't reset on loss.
- (`Assets/Scripts/Helper/Memory.cs` — a "move to Memory" comment the reviewer withdrew himself: "Ops, sorry! My bad.")

**What actually landed on the branch:** **Nothing.** There are zero commits on the PR after the review — the only commit is the original from before Oliver reviewed. The cooldown still resets on level completion **or loss** (5-min cooldown, `Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown`), which is exactly the lose-fast-to-reset exploit the reviewer described. The author deferred rather than fixed ("it does not matter if the player win or lose the level, we should sync with [EMPLOYEE_0016]") and it was merged as-is.

Category: author argued/deferred; nothing landed; objection (ad-gated upgrade exploit) still live in the build players are paying in.

⚠️ **Repo-state audit note** (recorded at Arthur's request ahead of the 2026-03-03 tooling shutdown — Combo Fighter is still live). Tracking ticket: **ENG-2438**.

This PR was **merged 2026-02-13 with a CHANGES_REQUESTED review from @oliver.brooks that was never converted to an approval** — nobody signed off after the changes were requested.

Reviewer's asks were on `ComboDefinition.cs` (`Locked` shouldn't be a serialized field → use a manager/PlayerPrefs-backed availability check; `LevelMultiplierRow` unnecessary; enum → `ERarityEnum`), `ComboScreen.cs` (`_specialPrefab` naming), `LockedComboCell.cs` (replace function-per-rarity with a `SerializedDictionary`), and `ComboRarityData/ComboRarityDefinition.cs` ("why do we need this?").

**Checked what actually landed (merge SHA `bf4e630`):** most of the code feedback *was* addressed in the follow-up commits — the `Locked` field is gone (now `IsLocked => !ComboManager.Instance.IsComboUnlocked(Id)`), the enum is `ERarityEnum`, and the prefab was consolidated. The `_specialPrefab` naming was **argued and resolved** (renamed `SpecialComboCell`), not ignored. So the code concerns look handled — they were just never re-reviewed.

**Still open:** (1) no reviewer re-approval on record; (2) the `ComboRarityDefinition` per-rarity unlock/leveling system introduced here was justified in review as coming from "Combo Unlocking Specs" — that spec is **not** in the GDD, the *Combo Fighter Design Details* workbook, the SHOP deck, or Confluence, and the shipped tiers dropped `Common` (contradicting the quoted numbers). Details in ENG-2438.

This PR was **merged 2026-01-30 with a CHANGES_REQUESTED review from @oliver.brooks that was never converted to an approval** (self-merged ~1 min after the last commit).

**Checked what actually landed (merge SHA `f065d1c`):**
- `Assets/Store/DominoPlayerPrefs.cs` — "Can we rename this?" → answered "Yes" and it **did land** (file renamed away from that path). ✅
- `ProfileScreen.cs` "missing `private`" → **landed**. ✅
- `ProfileScreen.cs` **"Looks dangerous"** (`_statPrefab` should be typed `ProfileStat` instead of a raw `GameObject` + `GetComponent`) → **NOT addressed.** `_statPrefab` is still a `GameObject`, and `AddStat()` still does `go.GetComponent<ProfileStat>()` then `stat.Init(...)` **with no null guard** — a misconfigured prefab now throws a NullReferenceException on the Profile screen. ❌ This objection is standing in the live build.

Recorded in ENG-2439.

Merged 2026-01-15 with a CHANGES_REQUESTED review from @oliver.brooks that was never approved, and **no commits were pushed after the review** — nothing changed between the objection and the merge.

The concern was a monetization one: the upgrade-ad cooldown resets on level completion **or loss**, so a player can enter a level, lose fast, return to the menu and watch another upgrade ad again. Oliver asked to move the reset (`Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset:true)` in `GameController.cs`) to WinScreen so it doesn't reset on a loss. The branch shows only the original pre-review commit; the author deferred instead of fixing. **The lose-fast-to-re-watch exploit is live in the current build.** Recorded in ENG-2440.

Confirmed it's a deterministic tool bug — the issue-comment endpoint hardcodes the same row ID, so only the first PR comment (on #37) could be posted. The durable record (the ENG tickets) is complete for all four, which was Arthur's stated goal ("so it survives past Slack"). I'll be transparent about this in the summary.

Now posting the summary to #prototype.

input.text:
*Combo Fighter repo — state of play (audit for Arthur, before Mar 3)*

Went through every PR on `harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters`. Only *human* review pushback counts here (CodeRabbit noted separately). Findings split the way you asked. Full detail + files are in the ENG tickets so it survives past Slack.

*⚠️ One tooling note first:* the "comment on the PR" step only worked on one PR — the GitHub comment tool is throwing a duplicate-key error after the first post, so I could only land the note on #37. The full per-PR write-up is in the ENG tickets below (which was the durable record you wanted anyway). Flagging so you're not surprised the PR threads are bare.

*Merged clean — reviewer signed off before merge (leave alone):*
• *#24* (rewarded ads / IAP hooks) — Oliver requested changes twice, author responded, Oliver *APPROVED* before merge. Process working.
• *#21, #16, #9* — Oliver approved before merge.

*Merged with changes requested and NO one ever signing off afterward — the ones you wanted on paper:*

*1) Reviewer ignored / objection still LIVE in the build*
• *#26 — upgrade-ad cooldown* → *ENG-2440.* Oliver flagged a monetization exploit: the ad-gated upgrade cooldown resets on level completion *or loss*, so a player can enter a level, lose fast, bounce to the menu and watch another upgrade ad again. He asked to move the reset out of `GameController.cs` into WinScreen. *Zero commits landed after his review* — nothing changed. Author deferred ("doesn't matter if you win or lose, let's sync with [teammate]") and it merged as-is. *This exploit is live right now.*
• *#35 — Blake/backend* → *ENG-2439.* Three review points on `ProfileScreen.cs` / `DominoPlayerPrefs.cs`. Two landed (file rename you said "Yes" to ✅, missing `private` ✅). The third did *not*: Oliver flagged `_statPrefab` as a raw `GameObject` + `GetComponent<ProfileStat>()` as dangerous and asked for a typed field. It's still untyped with *no null guard*, so a misconfigured prefab throws a NullReferenceException on the Profile screen. Merged (self-merge) ~1 min after the last commit, no re-review.

*2) Author argued the point — code got fixed, but never re-approved*
• *#37 — Combo Definition Updates* → *ENG-2438.* Oliver requested a pile of changes on `ComboDefinition.cs` (drop the serialized `Locked` field, `ERarityEnum` naming, etc.), `ComboScreen.cs`, `LockedComboCell.cs`, `ComboRarityDefinition.cs`. I checked the merge SHA: *most of it actually got fixed* in the "Addressed PR review" commits — `Locked` is gone (now a manager-backed `IsLocked`), enum is `ERarityEnum`, prefab consolidated. The `_specialPrefab` naming was *argued and resolved* (renamed `SpecialComboCell`), not ignored. So: code handled, just never re-reviewed. *But see the spec problem below* — this is the PR that worries me most on the design side.

*3) Looked bad, was actually fine (checked the branch, not the status)*
• *#19 — anim sequence on combo changed* → *ENG-2441.* Oliver flagged an IndexOutOfRange in `ElectricityController.cs`. No approval on record — but he *fixed it himself* ("fixing null refs") and merged. The bad index access is gone in the shipped code. Not a standing objection; logged only for completeness.

*"Agreed to a change, then it never landed" (the worst kind):* I looked specifically for this. I did *not* find a clean case — where someone said yes/OK and it then vanished. The rename you approved in #35 *did* land. The closest things are the two live objections in group 1 above, but those were deferred/ignored, not agreed-then-dropped.

*Design side — the spec check (this is the important one):*
You were right to be unsure. In #37 the combo *rarity + unlock-cost + per-rarity leveling* system was justified in review as coming from "Combo Unlocking Specs" (e.g. Common 100/200/300, Rare 150/300/450). *That spec does not exist in writing.* I checked the GDD, the "Combo Fighter Design Details" workbook (incl. the Combo List / Combo Sheet tabs), the SHOP deck, and Confluence — none of them define combo rarities, unlock costs, or per-rarity level-up requirements. The GDD explicitly treats every combo as *always available*, differentiated only by a designer-set bonus multiplier. The rarity tiers only ever existed as an informal chat in here back in Jan (Rare/Legendary/Mythical/Epic, and we even debated whether "Common" needs a label). The shipped build then *dropped Common entirely* (final #37 commit "Removed Common rarity"), so it doesn't even match the numbers that were quoted in the review. Net: the live combo-unlock/monetization system was built off a Slack thread, not an approved spec.

*Two extras worth a look:*
• *#34 (IAP)* merged with *zero review* — both you and Oliver were requested as reviewers and neither review was ever submitted. Live monetization code, unreviewed.
• *#18* — CodeRabbit (not a person) flagged a real one that was never rebutted: `ReduceIntervalBetweenCombos` is missing from the `HandleSkillAcquired` switch, so acquiring that skill won't re-record peak DPS. Not human review, so no ticket, but flagging it.

Tickets ENG-2438/2439/2440/2441 are all unassigned and in Backlog per your note (recording state, not committing anyone).
